The check refuses an export when a **business return’s EIN is already attached to another client in the same firm**, and that tax preparation has at least one shared automation `Document` record.

The local helper chain is:

1. [`perform`](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:53) prepares the payload and calls `validate_ein_already_sent!` before document validation or provider sending.
2. [`prepare_params`](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:137) determines whether the return is a business return and retains the EIN only for business returns. The default return type is `1040`.
3. [`already_sent_bound_account_id`](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:116) skips personal returns. For business returns, it looks for tax preparations matching:
   - the current **firm ID**;
   - the payload’s **EIN**;
   - a **different client ID**;
   - an ID referenced by `TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Document`.

That lookup has **no tax-year, return-type, provider, contact, upload-status, or processing-status filter**. Another firm’s matching EIN cannot block the export; another year or provider within the same firm can. The current client’s own records are excluded. If several records qualify, descending tax-preparation ID selects the bound client.

[`validate_ein_already_sent!`](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:111) raises `BoundAccountError` when that client ID is present. [`already_sent_error`](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:128) builds an `:unprocessable` general error with the `business_tax_identifier_already_sent` message and `bound_account_id`; `perform` rescues it and returns failure.

No files were edited.
